headline: Thursday's flight-to-quality bid got refunded in a day — the whole curve reset +4bp with the 10-year back at 5.00% and WTI at $103 — and this time it was the crowded defensive hideouts, not the semis, that paid for it.
summary: The bond rally lasted one session. Every tenor on the board rose 4bp: 2s to 4.69%, 5s 4.82%, 10s exactly 5.00%, 30s 5.33%, with the 10-year real yield at 2.66% and up 73bp year-to-date. The 30-year mortgage sits at 7.32%, 94th percentile, +37bp on the month. The proximate cause was crude: WTI jumped 4.0% to $103.44 while Brent fell 1.3% to $111.66, so the grade gap compressed again to roughly $8.2 from $9.0 — this is US barrels being bid, not seaborne premium being paid. Oil/gold is +5.3% today, +20.9% on the month, and pinned at the 100th percentile of its year. The inflation twist is unchanged and ugly: 5-year breakevens 2.48% (+14bp on the month, z=0.61) against 10-year breakevens 2.34% (-1bp). Inflation composite -47. With the Fed meeting next week and futures carrying meaningful odds of a December hike, the front end is not going to rescue anyone.

What actually changed is where the pain landed. Yesterday the tape was an AI de-rating with a defensive bid underneath it. Today the defensive bid broke. XLP fell 1.9% — the worst sector on the board — after a +7.1% month at z=1.80 with acceleration 2.21. XLU -0.7%, XLV -1.1%, SPLV -1.0%, USMV -0.5%, XLF -1.3%, DJI -1.2%, equal-weight -0.8%. Meanwhile NDX was flat, QQQ/SPY rose 0.5%, SMH +0.7%, SOXX +0.5%, MU +2.5%, AMD +1.7%, TSM +1.5%, and SMH/SPY printed +1.3% — the first leadership day for semis after a -11.4% relative month. EWY +1.5% off a 1-month z of -2.22, EWT +0.9%. Energy was the only sector green: XLE +2.6%, OIH +5.4%, XOP +2.4%, XOM +2.8%, CVX +2.9%, both majors at the 100th percentile. That is not risk-on. It is the duration tax arriving at the most crowded trade in the market while the de-rated stuff stops going down.

The relief is real but narrow. MOVE fell 3.3% to 103.31 with acceleration -0.74 — bond vol cooling while yields rise is repricing, not flight, and that is the single cleanest improvement versus yesterday's panic read. Copper added 2.1% to 6.4975, copper/gold +3.4% to a fresh 52-week high, DBC at the 100th percentile: the cycle pulse is not confirming a recession. Gasoline is still -12.8% on the month at z=-1.27 despite WTI's +12.2%, which is the pump disinflation that keeps CPI survivable. Against that, equity vol is still bid — VIX +2.2% to 19.45, VIX/VIX3M at 0.9497 with z=1.49 and acceleration 1.05, SKEW 151.8 — and credit is quietly worse, not better. HYG/IEF is -2.2% on the month at z=-1.63 with acceleration -1.32, HYG sits at the 36th percentile, BKLN at z=-1.06. The AI capex-debt story is now leaking into junk, and that is the transmission channel to watch, not the Nasdaq.

Dispersion is where the money is. The precious liquidation keeps going: gold 4010 (-7.1% month, 3.6th percentile), silver 53.96 (-16.2% month, z=-1.83), gold/silver +10.8% with acceleration 1.37, NEM -4.6% in a session, GDXJ -18.1% on the month. The AI-power and hard-asset complex remains the wreck: REMX -25.2%, URA -18.8%, NLR -16.6%, COPX -16.0%, XME -12.1% on the month, GEV -14.4%, ETN at z=-2.44. The consumer bellwethers cracked today too — TGT -3.4%, UBER -3.4%, NKE -2.7%, HD -2.4%, MCD -1.7% — with XLY/XLP at the 1st percentile of its 52-week range, a ratio that is now statistically absurd. And EM has split cleanly: Brazil is a bull market (EWZ +1.8% today, +14.0% on the month, BVSP z=1.73, USDBRL -2.6%) while Mexico is a debasement tape (USDMXN z=2.87, +7.9% on the month, 98th percentile) and China keeps bleeding (HSI -3.0%, Shanghai -1.5%, FXI at the 8th percentile).

good.text: MOVE fell 3.3% to 103.31 with acceleration -0.74 — bond vol cooled even as the entire curve reset 4bp higher. Yields rising without rate vol rising is repricing, not a liquidation.

Semis stopped going down. SMH +0.7%, SOXX +0.5%, SMH/SPY +1.3% after an -11.4% relative month, MU +2.5%, AMD +1.7%, TSM +1.5%, with EWY +1.5% off a 1-month z of -2.22 and EWT +0.9%. The Korea/Taiwan export channel of the de-rating is at least pausing.
Copper +2.1% to 6.4975 and copper/gold +3.4% to the 100th percentile of its year, with DBC also at the 100th percentile. The industrial complex is not pricing a demand collapse.

Energy is doing real index work: XLE +2.6%, OIH +5.4%, XOP +2.4%, XOM +2.8% and CVX +2.9% with both majors at the 100th percentile and +13.5% on the month. The only sector carrying earnings upgrades into a 5% 10-year.

Brazil keeps compounding: EWZ +1.8% to +14.0% on the month at z=1.59, BVSP z=1.73 at the 94th percentile, with USDBRL -1.1% today and -2.6% on the month. Equity up and currency up is the real thing, unlike Mexico.

Gasoline is -12.8% on the month at z=-1.27 despite WTI +12.2%, and USDCNY at 6.6606 sits at the very bottom of its 52-week range with USDKRW -2.0% on the month. Pump disinflation plus an anchored Asian FX complex takes two tail risks off the table.

bad.text: Parallel +4bp across the curve: 2s 4.69%, 10s back at exactly 5.00%, 30s 5.33%, 10-year real yield 2.66% and +73bp year-to-date. The 30-year mortgage at 7.32% is in the 94th percentile. Every discount-rate-sensitive asset pays this tax.

WTI +4.0% to $103.44, +80.1% year-to-date, and oil/gold +5.3% to the 100th percentile. 5-year breakevens at 2.48% (+14bp on the month) against 10-year breakevens at 2.34% is near-term inflation up, long-term growth down — the stagflationary twist, with the inflation composite at -47.

The hiding places broke. XLP -1.9% (worst sector, after +7.1% on the month at z=1.80, acceleration 2.21), XLU -0.7%, XLV -1.1%, SPLV -1.0%, USMV -0.5%, equal-weight -0.8%, Dow -1.2%. A crowded defensive trade unwinding is a faster, nastier drawdown than a tech de-rating because nobody is hedged for it.

Credit is deteriorating under the surface as AI capex debt gets repriced: HYG/IEF -2.2% on the month at z=-1.63 with acceleration -1.32, HYG at the 36th percentile, BKLN -0.8% on the month at z=-1.06, LQD -0.4% today. Spreads are widening while SPX is only -1.1% off — equities have not marked this.

Front-end vol stays bid: VIX +2.2% to 19.45 (+28.1% on the month, z=1.08), VIX/VIX3M at 0.9497 with z=1.49 and acceleration 1.05, SKEW 151.8. The term structure is flattening toward inversion into a Fed meeting and midterms.

The AI-power and hard-asset complex is still in free fall: REMX -25.2%, URA -18.8%, NLR -16.6%, COPX -16.0%, XME -12.1% on the month, GEV -14.4%, ETN at z=-2.44. Gold miners joined — NEM -4.6% in a session, GDXJ -18.1% on the month.

trades.name: Short long-end duration
trades.line: Short TLT: 10y back at 5.00%, oil $103, Dec hike in play
trades.expr: Short TLT at 81.34 outright, or buy TLT Dec 80 puts / sell Dec 85 calls for a zero-cost collar on the short. Futures alternative: short Dec 10-year note.
trades.thesis: Thursday's 17bp flight bid was a positioning event, not a policy repricing, and it was returned in one session. With WTI +12.2% on the month, 5-year breakevens +14bp and the 10-year real yield at 2.66%, the term premium story is intact and the long end has no cushion. MOVE falling 3.3% while yields rose tells you the panic buyer is gone.
trades.trigger: Whole curve +4bp today — 2s 4.69, 5s 4.82, 10s 5.00, 30s 5.33 — with WTI +4.0% to 103.44 and MOVE -3.3% at acceleration -0.74. TLT is still -2.4% below its 200-day and in a down trend despite being +1.5% on the month.
trades.stop: TLT closes above 83.5 (roughly a 10-year under 4.85), or HYG breaks 76 — a genuine credit event would make the growth scare, not the oil shock, the dominant bid.

trades.name: Oil services catch-up vs E&P
trades.line: Long OIH vs short XOP — services haven't marked $103 crude
trades.expr: Long OIH, short XOP, dollar-neutral, sized to roughly 1.0x beta on the ratio.
trades.thesis: E&P has fully priced $100 crude; the service complex has not. XOP is +10.4% on the month, 20.4% above its 200-day and at the 100th percentile of its year, while OIH is +0.4% on the month and 0.6% above its 200-day at the 69th percentile. If crude holds here, activity budgets follow and the laggard closes the gap; if crude breaks, you own the cheaper leg.
trades.trigger: OIH +5.4% today versus XOP +2.4% — the first clear day of service leadership, with WTI +4.0% and XLE +2.6% as the only green sector.
trades.stop: Ratio falls 5% from entry, or WTI closes below $95 (which would kill the activity thesis before the catch-up happens).
trades.target: 8-10% on the ratio, closing roughly half the 1-month performance gap.

trades.name: Fade the crowded staples bid
trades.line: Short XLP vs SPY: the defensive hideout just cracked
trades.expr: Short XLP, long an equal dollar amount of SPY. Options version: buy XLP Dec puts, sell SPY Dec puts of equal premium.
trades.thesis: Staples became the consensus hiding place: +7.1% on the month, +8.2% relative to the S&P, z=1.80 with acceleration 2.21, 89th percentile. That is a bond proxy bought on a rate-cut assumption that just got withdrawn, with a 10-year at 5.00% and a December hike live. Crowded defensives unwind faster than they accumulate.
trades.trigger: XLP -1.9% today, the single worst sector, on a day the Nasdaq was flat and semis led. XLU -0.7%, SPLV -1.0% and USMV -0.5% confirm the whole low-vol complex broke together, while SPHB/SPLV at z=-2.46 with acceleration -2.76 shows how stretched the rotation already is.
trades.stop: XLP relative strength versus SPY makes a new high, or the 10-year closes below 4.80% — that re-arms the bond-proxy bid.
trades.target: Give back half the +8.2% 1-month relative gain; XLP back toward 83.

trades.name: Tactical semiconductor bounce
trades.line: Long SMH: first semi leadership day off a z=-1.8 washout
trades.expr: Long SMH at 527, or December 540/600 call spread to cap risk on a counter-trend trade.
trades.thesis: The semi de-rating has been the dominant 2026 Q4 trade — SOXX -15.5% on the month at z=-1.83 with acceleration -1.93 — and it is now mature enough to produce a violent squeeze. Crucially SMH is still 2.4% above its 200-day and in an up trend; this is a de-rating of multiple, not a break of the price cycle.
trades.trigger: SMH/SPY +1.3% today, its first leadership print after -11.4% relative on the month; MU +2.5%, AMD +1.7%, TSM +1.5%, ASML +0.7%, with the Korea and Taiwan export proxies turning (EWY +1.5% off z=-2.22, EWT +0.9%) and QQQ/SPY +0.5%.
trades.stop: SOXX closes below last week's low, or SMH/SPY makes a new relative low — the ratio is the stop, not the price. AVGO, already -12.3% below its 200-day, breaking further is a second warning.
trades.target: SMH 575-585, retracing roughly half the -12.3% monthly drawdown.

trades.name: Latin America dispersion
trades.line: Long EWZ vs short EWW: BRL compounding, MXN at z=2.87
trades.thesis: Both markets look strong in local terms, but only one is paying you in dollars. Brazil has equity and currency moving together — EWZ +14.0% on the month, BVSP at the 94th percentile, USDBRL -2.6%. Mexico has equity up (+8.7% on the month) against a currency being destroyed: USDMXN +7.9% on the month at z=2.87 and the 98th percentile with acceleration 1.36. That combination is debasement, and the dollar-based ETF eventually marks it.
trades.trigger: EWZ +1.8% and USDBRL -1.1% today, versus EWW rolling over at -0.25% below its 200-day with USDMXN the single most stretched series on the board.
trades.stop: USDBRL back above 5.15, or the ratio gives back 6% from entry.

trades.name: Gold over silver
trades.line: Long GLD vs short SLV: ratio z=1.63 and accelerating
trades.expr: Long GLD, short SLV, matched by dollar notional. Futures version: long GC, short SI at the standard ratio.
trades.thesis: The precious liquidation is indiscriminate but silver is the leveraged leg, and its industrial bid is failing alongside the rest of the hard-asset complex. Gold/silver at 74.3 is +10.8% on the month with acceleration 1.37 and has room back toward the 80s if real yields keep rising at 2.66% and the metals unwind continues.
trades.trigger: Silver -1.5% today and -16.2% on the month at z=-1.83 versus gold -1.2% and -7.1%. The industrial confirmation is gone: XME -12.1%, COPX -16.0% on the month, GDXJ -18.1%.
trades.stop: Ratio closes below 70, or silver reclaims 58 — that would signal a genuine industrial re-bid rather than a liquidation bounce.

trades.name: High yield on AI debt contagion
trades.line: Buy HYG puts: AI capex debt is leaking into junk
trades.expr: Buy HYG January 75 puts, financed by selling the 71 strike. Alternative: short HYG, long IEF to isolate the spread.
trades.thesis: The equity market has treated the AI unwind as a multiple story. Credit is treating it as a leverage story. HYG/IEF is -2.2% on the month at z=-1.63 with acceleration -1.32 — a widening that is getting faster, not slower — while the S&P is only -1.1% off its month. Spreads lead equities at this stage of a capex cycle, and the hedge is cheap relative to how much index exposure it protects.
trades.trigger: HYG at the 36th percentile and rolling over, BKLN -0.8% on the month at z=-1.06, LQD -0.4% today, all while VIX/VIX3M at 0.9497 (z=1.49, acceleration 1.05) says the front end of the vol curve is already nervous.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF closes above its 1-month high, or HYG trades through 78 — that means the credit scare was a liquidity air pocket, not a default cycle.
